## Comparability note

All five companies report on a calendar fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), so the periods align [DOC-1]. However, **Alaska Air Group's FY2024 is not a clean like-for-like basis**: Alaska closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward, contributing $869 million of revenue (~7.4% of Alaska's $11,735M total) for roughly 3.5 months [DOC-2][DOC-1]. Alaska's ratios therefore blend a standalone Alaska full year with a partial-year, lower-margin Hawaiian stub, and the corresponding Hawaiian fuel and labor costs are not separately disclosed, so Alaska's percentages cannot be cleanly restated. Alaska's ranking (last and second-to-last) should be read with that caveat; the Delta/United/American/Southwest comparisons are directly comparable.

## Aircraft fuel expense as % of revenue, FY2024 (lowest first)

| Rank | Airline | Fuel / Revenue | Calculation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | **17.1%** | $10,566M / $61,643M [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | **20.6%** | $11,756M / $57,063M [DOC-1] |
| 3 | American | **21.1%** | $11,418M / $54,211M [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest | **21.1%** | $5,812M / $27,483M [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Alaska | **21.4%** | $2,506M / $11,735M [DOC-1][DOC-2] |

(American 21.06% vs. Southwest 21.15% — effectively a tie.)

## Salaries, wages and benefits as % of revenue, FY2024 (lowest first)

| Rank | Airline | Labor / Revenue | Calculation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | **26.2%** | $16,161M / $61,643M [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | **29.2%** | $16,678M / $57,063M [DOC-1] |
| 3 | American | **29.6%** | $16,021M / $54,211M [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Alaska | **30.6%** | $3,588M / $11,735M [DOC-1][DOC-2] |
| 5 | Southwest | **44.5%** | $12,240M / $27,483M [DOC-1] |

## Answer

Yes — **Delta ranks lowest (top-ranked) on both metrics**, at 17.1% fuel-to-revenue and 26.2% labor-to-revenue, consistent with its highest revenue base ($61,643M) and highest operating income ($5,995M) among the five [DOC-1]. United is second on both. The most notable divergence is Southwest, which sits mid-pack on fuel intensity but far highest on labor intensity (44.5%), consistent with its minimal $321M operating income [DOC-1].

ANSWER: Fuel % of revenue (lowest first): Delta 17.1%, United 20.6%, American 21.1%, Southwest 21.1%, Alaska 21.4%. Salaries/wages/benefits % of revenue (lowest first): Delta 26.2%, United 29.2%, American 29.6%, Alaska 30.6%, Southwest 44.5%. Yes — Delta is top-ranked (lowest) in both rankings; note Alaska's FY2024 includes Hawaiian only from Sept 18, 2024, so its ratios are not on a fully comparable basis.
